guidance: Explain briefly that the answer decides what kind of help fits the home. Do not argue, and do not suggest they leave or stay.
exampleLine: It tells us whether everyone can get out on their own, so we know what your home needs.

situation: Caller asks why the agent wants to know about their father's oxygen.

callerSays.en: Why does it matter that my dad uses oxygen?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué importa que mi papá use oxígeno?

guidance: Tie the question to what the responders need to know about the person's condition. Do not give medical advice or say how the oxygen will be handled.
exampleLine: It helps us know what your dad needs with him when he leaves the house.

situation: Caller asks why the agent needs the address again after they already gave it.

callerSays.en: Why do you need my address again? I already told you.
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué necesitan mi dirección otra vez? Ya se la di.

guidance: Explain that confirming the address keeps the call tied to the right home. Do not say anything was sent or that anyone is on the way.
exampleLine: Confirming it makes sure the call is tied to the right home.

situation: Caller asks why the agent wants to know whether water has come into the house.

callerSays.en: Why do you need to know if the water is inside the house?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué necesitan saber si el agua ya entró a la casa?

guidance: Say why the answer matters to getting out, and that this is what the agent is asking. Do not describe water levels, roads or conditions, because the prompt does not give them.
exampleLine: It tells us how hard it may be for your household to get out of the home.

situation: Caller asks why the agent needs to know about a pet and whether that changes anything.

callerSays.en: Why does it matter if we have a dog? Does that change anything?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué importa si tenemos un perro? ¿Eso cambia algo?

guidance: Answer the why only, since the code handles pet rules as its own policy. Do not say whether the dog can come, because that is a separate policy question the code answers.
exampleLine: It helps us understand everything your household needs to get out safely.

situation: Caller who is frightened asks why the agent is asking questions and whether they are in danger.

callerSays.en: Why are you asking all this? Are we going to drown?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué preguntan todo esto? ¿Nos vamos a ahogar?

guidance: Name the fear in a few words, then say honestly that you do not know the answer yet. Never say they are safe or will be fine, and do not add any new facts about the water.
exampleLine: That sounds frightening. I don't know that yet.

situation: Caller demands the agent stop asking questions and send someone instead of explaining.

callerSays.en: Stop asking why. Just send someone here now, please.
callerSays.es: Dejen de preguntar por qué. Manden a alguien ahora, por favor.

guidance: This is a plea for a ride, so flag it and do not answer with a reason or a time. Reflect their urgency in a few words and let the fixed status line respond.
exampleLine: You need help here quickly.

situation: Caller asks why the agent needs to know whether they can walk.

callerSays.en: Why do you need to know if I can walk?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué necesitan saber si puedo caminar?

guidance: Answer the why first and tie it to the vehicle they need. Do not promise a ride, a time or any help, and do not ask a question in the reply.
exampleLine: It helps us match the right vehicle to how you get around.

situation: Caller asks why the number of people in the home matters.

callerSays.en: Why do you need to know how many people are in the house?
callerSays.es: ¿Para qué necesitan saber cuántas personas hay en la casa?

guidance: Explain that the count sets the vehicle size. Never say or imply that anyone is coming or when.
exampleLine: The number of people tells us what size vehicle to match to your home.

situation: Caller asks why oxygen use matters for the trip.

callerSays.en: Why does it matter if we use oxygen?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué importa si usamos oxígeno?

guidance: Tie oxygen to the choice of vehicle, not to any promise of arrival. Do not repeat a misheard word, and do not name any medical outcome.
exampleLine: Oxygen equipment changes which vehicle fits your needs.

situation: Caller asks why pets are part of the call.

callerSays.en: Why do you care about my dog?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué les importa mi perro?

guidance: Explain pets as part of matching the vehicle to the home. Do not say whether a pet may ride along, because that is a policy question for the code to answer.
exampleLine: We ask about pets so we can match the right vehicle to your home.

situation: Caller asks why the wheelchair type matters.

callerSays.en: Does it matter if the wheelchair is electric?
callerSays.es: ¿Importa si la silla es eléctrica?

guidance: Confirm briefly that the kind of chair affects the vehicle, and name no time or outcome. Set the chair kind only if the caller actually says which kind it is.
exampleLine: Yes, the kind of chair helps us match the right vehicle.

situation: Caller asks why it matters that two people must lift someone.

callerSays.en: Why do you need to know if two people have to lift him?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué necesitan saber si dos personas tienen que levantarlo?

guidance: Tie the lifting need to the plan for moving him from the door to the vehicle. Do not mention crews, sending or what dispatchers are doing.
exampleLine: It lets us plan how he gets from the door to the vehicle.

situation: Caller says they are not leaving and asks why their information is needed.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving, so why do you need my info?
callerSays.es: No me voy, entonces ¿para qué necesitan mis datos?

guidance: Acknowledge the choice without arguing or guilting, and say the information is for matching a vehicle if they change their mind. Do not give any safety advice of your own.
exampleLine: Your answers help us match the right vehicle if you decide to go.

situation: Caller asks why the agent is asking for their address again.

callerSays.en: You already have my address, why ask again?
callerSays.es: Ya tienen mi dirección, ¿por qué preguntan otra vez?

guidance: Explain the check in terms of the right vehicle matching the right door. Do not imply that a vehicle is on its way.
exampleLine: We check it so the right vehicle matches the correct address.

situation: Caller asks why it matters whether they need a hand on the steps when they use a cane.

callerSays.en: Why does it matter whether someone helps me down the steps?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué importa si alguien me ayuda con los escalones?

guidance: Tie the steps question to matching the vehicle and planning the way to the door. Do not promise assistance, and do not state a timeline.
exampleLine: It tells us how to match the right vehicle and plan your way to the door.

situation: Caller asks why the agent wants to know if this is an earthquake, which the greeting did not name.

callerSays.en: Why are you asking, is this about an earthquake?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué preguntan, es por un terremoto?

guidance: Do not name or confirm a hazard the agent's own earlier words did not name; say plainly that the agent does not know that yet. Then tie the question back to the vehicle and the door.
exampleLine: I don't know that yet. Your answers help us match the right vehicle.

situation: Resident asks to speak to a real person about a wheelchair.

callerSays.en: Can I talk to a real person about my wheelchair?
callerSays.es: ¿Puedo hablar con una persona sobre mi silla de ruedas?

guidance: Say it is automated without offering a connection. The code's next question will ask about the wheelchair, so do not ask anything yourself.
exampleLine: I'm an automated assistant, but I can still learn what you need.

situation: Resident asks why an automated assistant needs to know their needs.

callerSays.en: Why does a robot need to know if I use a wheelchair?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué un robot necesita saber si uso silla de ruedas?

guidance: Confirm it is automated and tie the question to their need, without naming any vehicle or promising anything.
exampleLine: I'm automated. Knowing about your wheelchair matters for your needs.

situation: Resident asks whether anyone is actually listening to the call.

callerSays.en: Is anybody actually listening to this, or is it just a machine?
callerSays.es: ¿Hay alguien escuchando esto o es solo una máquina?

guidance: Say it is automated and that dispatchers work with it on this call. Do not promise anyone is listening in time or will act.
exampleLine: I'm automated, and dispatchers work with me on this call.

situation: Caller confirms the address the agent read back.

callerSays.en: Yes, that's our house.
callerSays.es: Sí, esa es nuestra casa.

guidance: Treat this as a yes to the address check. Reflect the confirmation in a few words and list no address change. Do not ask a question.
exampleLine: Mm-hm, that's the address we have.

situation: Caller says they are frightened because water is rising in the yard.

callerSays.en: The water is in the yard and I'm scared.
callerSays.es: El agua está en el patio y tengo miedo.

guidance: Name the feeling in a few words, then move on to the next question. Do not offer comfort that could be false, such as saying it will be fine.
exampleLine: That sounds frightening. I'll ask just a few quick questions.

situation: Caller asks whether the flood will reach their street.

callerSays.en: Is the river going to flood our street?
callerSays.es: ¿El río va a inundar nuestra calle?

guidance: Answer what they asked first and say plainly when you don't know. Never guess about the river, the water level or timing.
exampleLine: I don't know that yet, and I won't guess about the river.

situation: Caller demands a specific pickup time.

callerSays.en: When is the bus coming? Give me a time.
callerSays.es: ¿Cuándo llega el autobús? Dígame una hora.

guidance: Never give a time or promise a pickup. The code's status line answers ride questions, so keep the reply to effort and presence on the line.
exampleLine: I can't give you a time. I'm staying on the line with you.

situation: Caller cannot hear the agent and asks for a repeat.

callerSays.en: Hello? I didn't hear that. Can you say it again?
callerSays.es: ¿Hola? No escuché eso. ¿Puede repetirlo?

guidance: Acknowledge the request briefly and say you will repeat it in shorter parts. Do not add new information or a new question.
exampleLine: Sorry about that. I'll say it again, one part at a time.

situation: Background sound such as a TV is picked up by the phone.

callerSays.en: Turn that up, the weather man is on.
callerSays.es: Sube el volumen, ya salió el del tiempo.

guidance: This is not directed at the agent, so mark it not_to_agent and change nothing. Nothing is spoken back, so the example line is empty.

situation: Speech-to-text hears a misheard word right after the agent asked about oxygen.

callerSays.en: My mother needs autism to breathe.
callerSays.es: Mi madre necesita autismo para respirar.

guidance: After an oxygen question, read the word as oxygen, list medical with it, and list the field in guessed. Never say the misheard word back. Nothing is spoken for the echo, so the example line is empty.

situation: Caller asks the agent to switch to Spanish.

callerSays.en: Can you speak Spanish, please?
callerSays.es: ¿Puede hablar en español, por favor?

guidance: Set the language to es and keep the reply in the new language. Keep it short and do not repeat the earlier question yet.
exampleLine: Of course. We can continue in Spanish.

situation: Caller is trapped on a roof as water rises, with a family member.

callerSays.en: The water's up to the ceiling, I'm on the roof with my dad.
callerSays.es: El agua llega al techo, estoy en la azotea con mi papá.

guidance: Set the emergency as flames because they are trapped, so the code marks it urgent. Keep the reply to one calm line with no reassurance and no mention of help being sent.
exampleLine: That's urgent, and I'm staying on the line with you.

situation: Caller says they can't walk far and asks nothing, which is a plain answer to the agent's question about leaving on their own.

callerSays.en: No, my knees won't let me walk far.
callerSays.es: No, mis rodillas no me dejan caminar lejos.

guidance: Because canLeave is set, the code speaks its own echo, so the ack is empty. Do not add advice or promises.

situation: Caller refuses to leave without a pet and the record has no canLeave yet.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving without my dog.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi perro.

guidance: Acknowledge the choice in the caller's own words without arguing or guilting them. Setting canLeave to unsure is the code's job, so only the ack is needed here.
exampleLine: You won't leave without your dog. I hear that.

situation: Caller pleads with the agent to hurry while the shaking continues.

callerSays.en: Please, the house is still shaking, hurry!
callerSays.es: Por favor, la casa todavía tiembla, ¡apúrense!

guidance: Flag asks_ride for the plea and reflect their urgency without any promise of arrival or timing. Do not repeat back a demand for speed as if it will be met.
exampleLine: You want us to hurry, and the house is still shaking.

situation: Caller anxiously asks whether anyone knows they are still inside.

callerSays.en: Does anyone know we're still in here?
callerSays.es: ¿Alguien sabe que seguimos aquí adentro?

guidance: Flag asks_ride and feeling, name the fear in a few words, and reflect the question without saying that anyone is coming or that they are safe.
exampleLine: That sounds frightening. You want to know we know you're here.

situation: Caller reports someone injured by falling objects during the quake.

callerSays.en: My husband's bleeding, the bookshelf fell on him.
callerSays.es: Mi esposo está sangrando, la estantería se le cayó encima.

guidance: Set emergency to medical and flag the injury immediately. Reflect what they said and do not give first-aid advice, since the code gives the only advice.
exampleLine: You're telling me your husband is bleeding and the bookshelf fell on him.

situation: Caller asks why the agent needs to know whether everyone can walk out.

callerSays.en: Why do you need to know if we can walk out?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué necesitan saber si podemos salir caminando?

guidance: Answer the why in one calm sentence tied to their needs. Do not mention help, vehicles or sending, and do not ask a question.
exampleLine: It tells us how to plan for everyone in your home.

situation: Caller asks to switch the call to Spanish.

callerSays.en: Español, por favor.
callerSays.es: Español, por favor.

guidance: Set language to es and flag nothing else. Confirm the switch in Spanish in a few words without any promise.
exampleLine: Claro, seguimos en español.

situation: Caller says they didn't hear the question after an aftershock and asks the agent to repeat it.

callerSays.en: Sorry, what? I didn't catch that.
callerSays.es: Perdón, ¿qué? No le entendí.

guidance: Flag asks_repeat only, with no changes and no ack or reply, so the code repeats the question. Do not restate the question yourself.

situation: Caller answers the head-count question but mid-sentence reports chest pain and trouble breathing in someone at home.

callerSays.en: Two of us, but my husband's chest is hurting, he can't catch his breath.
callerSays.es: Somos dos, pero el pecho de mi esposo le duele, no puede respirar bien.

guidance: Set peopleCount=2 and emergency=medical, since the answer still counts. Don't tell them to call 911, and don't add advice beyond the fixed lines.
exampleLine: His chest pain is serious, and that's urgent.

situation: Caller says a family member on oxygen is in distress, and speech-to-text turns the word oxygen into autism after the agent asked about oxygen.

callerSays.en: She desperately needs autism, the machine just stopped and she's gasping.
callerSays.es: Ella necesita desesperadamente autismo, la máquina se paró y está jadeando.

guidance: Read autism as oxygen, list medical=oxygen with guessed=medical=oxygen so the read-back checks it, and set emergency=medical. Never say the misheard word back.
exampleLine: Her oxygen machine stopped, and that's urgent.

situation: Caller reports a fall and a suspected broken hip in someone who can't get up, while the agent is asking about mobility.

callerSays.en: He fell in the bathroom, I think his hip is broken, he can't move his leg.
callerSays.es: Se cayó en el baño, creo que se rompió la cadera, no puede mover la pierna.

guidance: Set emergency=medical because someone is hurt now. Name the injury plainly and don't promise any help or timing.
exampleLine: A possible broken hip is serious, and it's urgent.

situation: Caller says water is rising in the house and they are stuck in the attic with no way down.

callerSays.en: The water's coming up the hallway and we're stuck in the attic, we can't get down.
callerSays.es: El agua está subiendo por el pasillo y estamos atrapados en el ático, no podemos bajar.

guidance: Trapped people are the flames category in the emergency field, so set emergency=flames. Don't guess about water levels or rescue; only say they are trapped and it's urgent.
exampleLine: You're trapped, and that's urgent.

situation: Caller says outright that they don't think they will make it out of the home in time.

callerSays.en: I don't think we're going to make it out, the water's already at the door.
callerSays.es: No creo que vayamos a salir a tiempo, el agua ya está en la puerta.

guidance: Set emergency=flames because they say they won't make it. Acknowledge the fear in a few words, without comfort that could be false or any promise.
exampleLine: That's urgent, and I can hear how scared you are.

situation: Caller mid-answer says they're getting in the car, then breaks off to report someone collapsed on the floor and not breathing.

callerSays.en: We're getting in the car now, wait, my mom's on the floor and she's not breathing.
callerSays.es: Ya nos subimos al carro, espere, mi mamá está en el piso y no está respirando.

guidance: Set canLeave=yes for the car, and emergency=medical for the collapse. The emergency does not replace the answer, and the agent should not give CPR or other instructions.
exampleLine: Your mom isn't breathing, and that's urgent.

situation: Caller reports dizziness and vomiting after running a generator indoors during the storm.

callerSays.en: My husband's dizzy and throwing up, we ran the generator in the garage because the power's out.
callerSays.es: Mi esposo está mareado y vomitando, pusimos el generador en el garaje porque se fue la luz.

guidance: Set emergency=medical because someone is ill now. Don't diagnose or tell them what to do about the generator; the code gives the only advice.
exampleLine: Dizziness and vomiting for him is serious, and it's urgent.

situation: Caller misses dialysis, and the person is confused and swelling, the agent having asked about dialysis earlier.

callerSays.en: He missed his dialysis today, he's confused and his legs are all swollen.
callerSays.es: Se perdió su diálisis hoy, está confundido y las piernas se le hincharon.

guidance: Set medical=dialysis and emergency=medical because the confusion and swelling are a medical emergency now. Don't claim anything about when treatment is available.
exampleLine: Missed dialysis with confusion is serious, and that's urgent.

situation: Caller describes water at the door and wants to stay, with no one hurt and nobody trapped.

callerSays.en: The water's at the door but we're all fine, we're staying, nobody's hurt.
callerSays.es: El agua está en la puerta pero todos estamos bien, nos quedamos, nadie está herido.

guidance: No emergency, since nobody is hurt or trapped. Set canLeave=unsure because they won't leave, and respect the choice without arguing.
exampleLine: You're choosing to stay, and I've heard that.

situation: Caller says someone needs help being moved right now, and they can't stand or walk at all.

callerSays.en: My dad can't stand up at all, we need two of us to lift him, the water's rising.
callerSays.es: Mi papá no puede pararse para nada, necesitamos dos personas para levantarlo, el agua está subiendo.

guidance: Set assistanceRequired=two_person_lift and mobility=bedbound only if they said bed; here set mobility=manual_wheelchair only if stated, otherwise leave it out. No emergency unless someone is hurt or trapped.
exampleLine: Two people to lift him, got it.

situation: Caller says they are frightened and asks whether anyone knows they are still there.

callerSays.en: I'm so scared. Does anyone know we're still here?
callerSays.es: Estoy muy asustada. ¿Saben que seguimos aquí?

guidance: Name the fear in a few words, then answer only what was asked. Do not say that anyone is coming or that anyone knows where they are; the code's status line handles the ride.
exampleLine: I can hear how scared you are. I'm still on the line with you.

situation: Caller pleads for speed in a frightened voice.

callerSays.en: Please hurry, please, we're really scared right now.
callerSays.es: Por favor, apúrense, por favor, estamos muy asustados.

guidance: Name the feeling, then reflect their urgency without promising a time or a vehicle. Never say help is on the way.
exampleLine: That sounds frightening. You need help fast.

situation: Caller says they are scared, but the agent already named a feeling in its previous turn.

callerSays.en: Yes, we're scared, and the kids are crying in the back.
callerSays.es: Sí, tenemos miedo, y los niños están llorando atrás.

guidance: The agent already named the feeling, so do not repeat it. Acknowledge the children briefly and move on to the next question.
exampleLine: Thanks, the children are with you now.

situation: Caller tells the agent not to risk anyone coming for them.

callerSays.en: Don't send anyone out for us, it's too dangerous.
callerSays.es: No manden a nadie por nosotros, es muy peligroso.

guidance: Name the worry about putting others at risk. Do not argue, do not promise anyone will come, and do not mention crews or sending.
exampleLine: I can hear you're worried about putting others at risk.

situation: Caller is crying because they feel they cannot leave a pet behind.

callerSays.en: I can't leave my cat, I'm crying, I can't do it.
callerSays.es: No puedo dejar a mi gato, estoy llorando, no puedo.

guidance: Name the sadness briefly and do not promise the pet can come. Do not give advice about pets; the code handles pet questions.
exampleLine: That sounds really hard, especially with your cat.

situation: Caller sounds calm and gives no sign of fear or distress.

callerSays.en: Yeah, we're fine, just gathering a few things.
callerSays.es: Sí, estamos bien, solo juntando algunas cosas.

guidance: No feeling is expressed, so name none and do not invent one. Give a plain short reflection of what they said.
exampleLine: Thanks, you're gathering a few things.

situation: Caller is frustrated and angry after waiting on the line.

callerSays.en: This is ridiculous, we've been waiting forever!
callerSays.es: ¡Esto es ridículo, llevamos muchísimo tiempo esperando!

guidance: Name the frustration in a few words. Do not give a long apology, do not say how long the wait will be, and do not tell them to wait.
exampleLine: That sounds maddening, waiting like this.

situation: Caller is sobbing and the speech-to-text is only partly readable.

callerSays.en: Sorry... I can't... he won't... I just can't.
callerSays.es: Perdón... no puedo... él no quiere... simplemente no puedo.

guidance: Since the words are only partly clear, name only the distress they can hear, not a specific fear. Do not guess what the person said.
exampleLine: I can hear that this is very hard right now.

situation: Caller says they will not leave without a family member and is upset about it.

callerSays.en: I won't leave without my son, I can't just go and leave him.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi hijo, no puedo irme y dejarlo.

guidance: Respect their choice without arguing or guilting them. Name how hard the choice feels and let the code continue. Do not say the son will be picked up.
exampleLine: That sounds like a very hard place to be in.

situation: Caller says water is already inside the home and still rising.

callerSays.en: The water's up to our knees in the kitchen and it's still coming in.
callerSays.es: El agua ya nos llega a las rodillas en la cocina y sigue entrando.

guidance: Flag the emergency at once and reflect only the fact they gave. Do not tell them to move to a higher floor or leave, because the code gives any advice.
exampleLine: That's urgent, and I'm staying on the line with you.

situation: Caller says a person is trapped in the attic as the water climbs.

callerSays.en: My mom is stuck in the attic and the water is still going up.
callerSays.es: Mi mamá está atrapada en el ático y el agua sigue subiendo.

guidance: Treat as trapped and flag urgent. Do not promise anyone will reach her or when; say only what they told you.
exampleLine: Your mom is in the attic and the water is rising. That's urgent.

situation: Caller says someone is not breathing properly and the oxygen stopped when the power went out.

callerSays.en: He's not breathing right and turning blue, and the power's out so his oxygen stopped.
callerSays.es: No respira bien, se está poniendo azul, y se fue la luz así que se paró su oxígeno.

guidance: Flag medical immediately, even before the rest of the answer. Set medical=oxygen only if the answer clearly fits, and never tell them to call 911.
exampleLine: I hear that he can't breathe. That's urgent.

situation: Caller says a child went into fast water outside the house.

callerSays.en: My little boy went out to the street and the current took him.
callerSays.es: Mi hijito salió a la calle y la corriente se lo llevó.

guidance: Flag urgent and name the fear briefly. Do not say anyone is going after him or how soon.
exampleLine: That's urgent. I can hear how scared you are.

situation: Caller says an adult on the roof has severe chest pain.

callerSays.en: My husband climbed onto the roof and now his chest hurts really bad.
callerSays.es: Mi esposo subió al techo y ahora le duele mucho el pecho.

guidance: Flag medical urgent. Do not diagnose or tell them how to position him; keep the reply to what they said.
exampleLine: Chest pain is urgent. Thank you for telling me that.

situation: Caller says they were shocked touching an appliance standing in floodwater.

callerSays.en: I touched the fridge while it was in the water and got shocked, my arm is numb.
callerSays.es: Toqué el refrigerador mientras estaba en el agua y me dio una descarga, tengo el brazo entumecido.

guidance: Flag urgent. Do not advise turning off power or moving; the code gives any such steps.
exampleLine: That's urgent. Thanks for telling me about your arm.

situation: Caller reports dizziness and headaches after running a generator indoors.

callerSays.en: We ran the generator in the garage and my head is pounding and everyone's dizzy.
callerSays.es: Pusimos el generador en el garaje y me duele la cabeza y todos estamos mareados.

guidance: Flag medical urgent. Do not advise shutting off the generator or opening windows; that belongs to the code's lines.
exampleLine: Dizziness and a pounding head are urgent. Thanks for telling me.

situation: Caller says they don't think they will make it out because the water is too high.

callerSays.en: Honestly we're not going to make it out, the water's too high.
callerSays.es: Honestamente no vamos a salir, el agua está demasiado alta.

guidance: Flag urgent under the won't-make-it rule. Do not promise safety or comfort that could be false; acknowledge what they said plainly.
exampleLine: I hear you think you won't make it. That's urgent.

situation: Caller starts an emergency mid-sentence while giving the household count.

callerSays.en: We have two people, my husband, he's on the floor bleeding and the water is...
callerSays.es: Somos dos, mi esposo está en el suelo sangrando y el agua está...

guidance: Flag the bleeding immediately without waiting for the sentence to finish. Set peopleCount=2 from the head count, and do not promise anything about help.
exampleLine: Bleeding is urgent. Thanks, that's two people in the home.

situation: Caller reports someone in floodwater across the street who is not in their home.

callerSays.en: There's a man yelling in the water across the street, he's not in our house.
callerSays.es: Hay un hombre gritando en el agua al otro lado de la calle, no está en nuestra casa.

guidance: Flag urgent. Record the location under neighbors rather than the household fields, and do not promise anyone can reach him.
exampleLine: That's urgent. Thanks for telling me where he is.

situation: Caller confirms the address the agent read back.

callerSays.en: Yes, that's our place, 1182 Mariposa.
callerSays.es: Sí, ahí vivimos, en 1182 Mariposa.

guidance: A confirmation counts as yes. Reflect what they agreed to instead of a bare okay, and list no address since it matches the record.
exampleLine: Alright, that's the address.

situation: Caller asks the agent to hold while they check with someone in the home.

callerSays.en: Hold on, let me ask my daughter.
callerSays.es: Déjame preguntarle a mi hija.

guidance: Set wants_time and reflect who they are checking with. Never tell them to wait or take their time, and never promise anything.
exampleLine: Sure, you're checking with your daughter.

situation: Caller says they won't leave without their pet.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving without my cat.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi gato.

guidance: Respect the choice without arguing or guilting them. Reflect their words, and let the code continue.
exampleLine: You won't leave without your cat.

situation: Caller pleads for someone to come quickly.

callerSays.en: Please hurry, please, we need someone here now.
callerSays.es: Por favor, apúrense, necesitamos a alguien aquí ya.

guidance: Set asks_ride and a feeling. Reflect the urgency in a few words and make no promise about who is coming or when.
exampleLine: You need help fast.

situation: Caller reports that a neighbor who may need help is across the street.

callerSays.en: The man across the street can't walk either.
callerSays.es: El señor de enfrente tampoco puede caminar.

guidance: List the location in neighbors, not set. Reflect the neighbor's situation and do not promise that anyone will go to him.
exampleLine: Across the street, he can't walk.

situation: Caller asks whether they can bring medical equipment.

callerSays.en: Can I bring my oxygen tank with me?
callerSays.es: ¿Puedo llevar mi tanque de oxígeno?

guidance: Set policy_question as a short English question. Reflect their concern. Reply with I don't know that, since the code supplies any approved answer.
exampleLine: You're asking about your oxygen tank.

situation: Caller on the line is away from home and gives the address of the person still there.

callerSays.en: I'm in the car, he's still at our house, 3037 Ewing Street.
callerSays.es: Estoy en el carro, él sigue en la casa, en 3037 Ewing Street.

guidance: Set address to the house address since the household is there. Reflect that the caller is away and someone is still home, without promising any ride.
exampleLine: Calling for someone still at home.

situation: Caller asks whether anyone knows they are there.

callerSays.en: Does anybody even know we're still here?
callerSays.es: ¿Alguien sabe que todavía estamos aquí?

guidance: Set asks_ride and a feeling. Reflect the question without saying anyone has been alerted or is coming.
exampleLine: You're asking if anyone knows.

situation: Caller reports flames in the yard next to their home.

callerSays.en: Flames are in my neighbor's yard right now.
callerSays.es: Hay llamas en el patio de mi vecino ahora mismo.

guidance: Set the flames emergency so the code marks it urgent. Reflect what they can see and do not say they are safe or give directions.
exampleLine: Flames are in your neighbor's yard.

situation: Caller reports being trapped by smoke inside the home.

callerSays.en: I think I'm trapped, the smoke is in the bedroom.
callerSays.es: Creo que estoy atrapada, hay humo en el dormitorio.

guidance: Set the flames emergency and a feeling, and flag it urgent for a dispatcher. Reflect the trap and smoke without any promise of rescue or safety.
exampleLine: You're trapped, smoke in the bedroom.

situation: Caller says they won't leave their home without their dog.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving without my dog.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi perro.

guidance: Acknowledge the choice in their own words and do not argue or guilt them. Set canLeave to unsure if the record has no canLeave yet, and let the code continue.
exampleLine: You won't leave without your dog. Thanks for telling me.

situation: Caller says they will stay in their house and won't go anywhere.

callerSays.en: I'm not going anywhere. I'm staying in my house.
callerSays.es: No me voy a ir a ningún lado. Me quedo en mi casa.

guidance: Reflect that they plan to stay home, without argument or a warning about danger. Do not promise anything about the ground or the building.
exampleLine: You've decided to stay in your home.

situation: Caller refuses to leave without a spouse who is away from the home.

callerSays.en: I won't leave without my husband, he's still at work.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi esposo, todavía está en el trabajo.

guidance: Acknowledge that they want to wait for their husband and do not guilt them. Do not guess when he will be home or say he is safe.
exampleLine: You want to wait for your husband.

situation: Caller says they won't leave because they want to watch over their property.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving my house empty. Somebody has to watch it.
callerSays.es: No voy a dejar mi casa vacía. Alguien tiene que cuidarla.

guidance: Respect the choice and do not argue about looting or property. Keep the reply to a short acknowledgment with no advice.
exampleLine: You want to keep an eye on your home.

situation: Caller says they already promised a neighbor they would stay put.

callerSays.en: I already told my neighbor I'd stay here with her.
callerSays.es: Ya le prometí a mi vecina que me quedaría aquí con ella.

guidance: Acknowledge the promise and the choice. Do not invent facts about the neighbor and do not suggest they are wrong to keep it.
exampleLine: You promised your neighbor you'd stay together.

situation: Caller refuses to leave and asks the agent to stop sending anyone for them.

callerSays.en: Don't send anyone for me. I'm staying, and I don't want anyone risked.
callerSays.es: No manden a nadie por mí. Me quedo y no quiero que arriesguen a nadie.

guidance: Name the feeling briefly, then respect the refusal without arguing. Never say or imply that help is coming or when.
exampleLine: You don't want anyone put at risk for you.

situation: Caller says their cat is hiding under the bed and they won't leave without it.

callerSays.en: My cat is under the bed. I'm not leaving without her.
callerSays.es: Mi gata está debajo de la cama. No me voy sin ella.

guidance: Acknowledge the cat and the choice without arguing. Do not promise that the cat can come or give advice on finding it.
exampleLine: You won't go without your cat.

situation: Caller says they won't leave because they don't want to be carried out of the house.

callerSays.en: I won't leave. I'm not letting anybody carry me out like a sack.
callerSays.es: No me voy. No voy a dejar que me saquen cargando como un costal.

guidance: Respect the refusal and their dignity, and take their word about their mobility. Do not argue or describe what will happen; set canLeave unsure only if the record has none.
exampleLine: You don't want to be carried out. I hear you.

situation: Caller first refuses to leave, then reverses and says they are going now.

callerSays.en: Never mind, we're getting in the car now.
callerSays.es: Olvídelo, nos estamos subiendo al carro ahora.

guidance: Set canLeave yes because they are leaving now. Reflect that they are going and do not repeat any promise about a ride.
exampleLine: You're getting in the car now.

situation: Caller refuses to leave and says they want to stay on the line only as long as no one is sent.

callerSays.en: I'm staying home. I just want to know nobody is being sent out for me.
callerSays.es: Me quedo en casa. Solo quiero saber que no están mandando a nadie por mí.

guidance: Acknowledge the choice and their concern about others without promising that nobody will be sent. This is a plea about a ride, so set asks_ride and do not answer the question with a promise.
exampleLine: You want to know no one is being sent for you.

situation: Caller refuses to leave and speaks Vietnamese, which the agent cannot yet read.

callerSays.en: I'm not going. I'm staying here with my family.
callerSays.es: No me voy. Me quedo aquí con mi familia.

guidance: If the words are garbled in English but look like Vietnamese, set language to vi and do not guess the content. Keep the reply empty and respect the choice when it can be understood.
exampleLine: You're staying here with your family.

situation: The caller asks why the assistant needs to know whether someone in the home can walk.

callerSays.en: Why do you need to know if he can walk?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué necesitan saber si él puede caminar?

guidance: Answer the why first, tied to the right vehicle and help at the door. Do not ask a question; the code asks the next one.
exampleLine: It helps us match the right vehicle to his needs.

situation: The caller asks whether someone is coming to pick them up.

callerSays.en: Is someone coming to get us? When will they be here?
callerSays.es: ¿Viene alguien a recogernos? ¿Cuándo llegará?

guidance: The code's fixed status line answers the ride question, so the reply is empty. The acknowledgment only reflects the caller's words and makes no promise of a vehicle or time.
exampleLine: You want to know when a ride will get there.

situation: The caller asks whether the assistant will stay on the line.

callerSays.en: Are you going to stay on the phone with me?
callerSays.es: ¿Se va a quedar en la línea conmigo?

guidance: This is answered directly in the reply, not as a ride question. Keep it to one short sentence and do not ask anything back.
exampleLine: Yes, I'm staying on the line with you.

situation: The caller asks what they should do while they wait.

callerSays.en: What should I do now? Should I pack anything?
callerSays.es: ¿Qué debo hacer ahora? ¿Debo empacar algo?

guidance: Set asks_what_to_do and leave the reply empty so the code gives its fixed steps. The acknowledgment reflects the question without advice of its own.
exampleLine: You want to know what to get ready while you wait.

situation: The caller asks whether their cat can come along to the vehicle.

callerSays.en: Can I bring my cat with me?
callerSays.es: ¿Puedo llevar a mi gato conmigo?

guidance: Record the policy question in plain English and answer with the approved 'I don't know that.' unless the code has its own answer. Never guess about pets being allowed.
exampleLine: I don't know that.

situation: The caller is frightened and asks whether anyone knows they are there.

callerSays.en: Does anybody know we're still here? Please, I'm so scared.
callerSays.es: ¿Alguien sabe que todavía estamos aquí? Por favor, tengo mucho miedo.

guidance: Name the feeling briefly and reflect their question without promising that anyone knows or is coming. Set the flags for the ride question and the plea.
exampleLine: You want to know they know you're here.

situation: The caller asks the assistant to wait while they check with someone else.

callerSays.en: Hold on, let me ask my daughter.
callerSays.es: Espere, déjeme preguntarle a mi hija.

guidance: Set wants_time. Reflect that they are checking with someone, and do not tell them to take their time or to wait.
exampleLine: You're checking with your daughter first.

situation: The caller asks whether the storm will reach their house.

callerSays.en: Is the hurricane going to hit our house?
callerSays.es: ¿El huracán va a golpear nuestra casa?

guidance: The assistant does not know the storm's path from this prompt, so it must say so plainly and not guess about the hazard, timing or roads.
exampleLine: I don't know that yet.

situation: The background sound of a TV or another person in the room is picked up as speech.

callerSays.en: Honey, grab the dog and the bags from the hall.
callerSays.es: Cariño, agarra al perro y las bolsas del pasillo.

guidance: This is not the resident talking to the assistant, so set not_to_agent with no changes, and leave ack and reply empty.

situation: Caller asks whether someone is coming to get them.

callerSays.en: Is someone coming to pick us up?
callerSays.es: ¿Viene alguien a recogernos?

guidance: This is an asks_ride flag, so the assistant reflects the caller's question without any promise and gives no reply line, because the code's fixed status line answers the ride question. It must not say a driver or vehicle is coming or give any time.
exampleLine: You want to know about the ride.

situation: Caller asks whether the agent will stay on the line.

callerSays.en: Will you stay on the line with me?
callerSays.es: ¿Se queda en la línea conmigo?

guidance: The caller asks a yes-or-no question about staying on the line, which is not a ride request, so the reply answers it directly. The assistant must not promise anything about help or timing beyond staying on the line.
exampleLine: Yes, I'm staying on the line with you.

situation: Caller asks why the agent needs to know whether they can walk.

callerSays.en: Why do you need to know if we can walk out?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué necesita saber si podemos salir caminando?

guidance: The caller asks why, so the reply answers the why first, tied to the right vehicle and help at the door. The assistant must not invent details about routes or shelters and must not ask a question.
exampleLine: It helps us match the right vehicle to your needs.

situation: Caller says they need a moment to check with someone else first.

callerSays.en: Hold on, let me ask my daughter.
callerSays.es: Espere, déjeme preguntarle a mi hija.

guidance: This is a wants_time flag, so the assistant reflects that they are checking with someone and gives no reply. It must not tell them to take their time or to wait, and must not ask a question.
exampleLine: You're checking with your daughter first.

situation: Caller asks whether they are supposed to evacuate now.

callerSays.en: Are we supposed to evacuate right now?
callerSays.es: ¿Se supone que evacuemos ahora mismo?

guidance: The caller asks a direct question, so the reply gives the only safety line the assistant may use and the code continues the call. The assistant may say a warning covers their street only if the agent's greeting already said so, and must give no directions of its own.
exampleLine: If you can leave safely, leave now.

situation: Caller asks whether they can bring their pet along.

callerSays.en: Can I bring my cat with us?
callerSays.es: ¿Puedo llevar a mi gato con nosotros?

guidance: This is a policy question, so the reply is the honest unknown answer, and policy_question is set with the English question 'Can I bring my cat?' The assistant must not guess the shelter's rules.
exampleLine: I don't know that.

situation: Caller asks what they should do or pack while they wait.

callerSays.en: What should I do now? Should I pack anything?
callerSays.es: ¿Qué debo hacer ahora? ¿Debo empacar algo?

guidance: This is an asks_what_to_do flag, so the code gives its own fixed steps and the assistant gives no reply. The acknowledgment only reflects that they want to know what to do, with no advice of its own.
exampleLine: You want to know what to do next.

situation: Caller asks whether the ride costs money.

callerSays.en: Is the ride going to cost us anything?
callerSays.es: ¿Cuánto cuesta el viaje?

guidance: This is a policy question about cost, so policy_question is set as 'How much does the ride cost?' in English and the reply is the honest unknown answer in the caller's language. The assistant must not state a price or claim the ride is free.
exampleLine: I don't know that.

situation: Resident says they will not leave without their cat.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving without my cat.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi gato.

guidance: Acknowledge the pet and the choice without arguing or guilt. Set canLeave to unsure if none is recorded yet, and do not promise anything about the pet. The code continues.
exampleLine: You won't leave without your cat. I heard you.

situation: Resident says they won't go until an adult son who is out of the home gets back.

callerSays.en: I won't go without my son. He's not home yet.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi hijo. Todavía no llega a casa.

guidance: Reflect that they want their son with them. Do not tell them to wait or promise when he will return, and do not argue about the warning.
exampleLine: You want your son with you before you go.

situation: Resident says they will not leave their own home.

callerSays.en: This is my house. I'm not leaving it.
callerSays.es: Es mi casa. No la voy a dejar.

guidance: Name that it is their home and accept the refusal without lecturing. Keep the reply short and do not describe the fire or the roads.
exampleLine: That's your home, and you've said you're staying.

situation: Resident flatly refuses to leave and says they have decided.

callerSays.en: No, I'm staying here. I've made up my mind.
callerSays.es: No, me quedo aquí. Ya lo decidí.

guidance: Acknowledge the decision in their words. Do not repeat the warning or try to change their mind, and let the code move on.
exampleLine: Alright, you've made your decision.

situation: Resident says they won't leave because they fear their belongings will be stolen.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving. People will steal everything I own.
callerSays.es: No me voy. Me van a robar todo lo que tengo.

guidance: Name the worry in their words without offering comfort that might be false. Do not argue about the risk, and do not say anything about police or patrols.
exampleLine: You're worried about losing your things.

situation: Resident refuses to leave after an earlier answer already recorded that they cannot leave.

callerSays.en: I'm not going anywhere, I told you already.
callerSays.es: No me voy a ningún lado, ya se lo dije.

guidance: A refusal never replaces a recorded no, so canLeave stays no and is not changed to unsure. Thank them for telling the agent and do not argue.
exampleLine: Thank you for telling us again. You've said you're staying.

situation: Resident refuses to leave while a flame emergency is close to the home.

callerSays.en: There's ash on the porch, but I'm not going anywhere.
callerSays.es: Hay ceniza en el porche, pero no me voy a ningún lado.

guidance: Flag the emergency as flames because embers are next to the home. Respect the refusal without arguing or guilt, and keep the reply to what the caller said.
exampleLine: You've said you're staying, and the ash is right by you.

situation: Resident says they will leave only when they feel ready, not when the call tells them to.

callerSays.en: I'll go when I'm ready, not before.
callerSays.es: Me voy cuando yo esté lista, no antes.

guidance: Respect their timing and do not push. Do not set a time or tell them to hurry, and do not mention any help or vehicle.
exampleLine: You want to go when you're ready. That's your call.

situation: Resident refuses to leave and asks whether help will still come for them if they stay.

callerSays.en: If I stay, will someone still come get me?
callerSays.es: Si me quedo, ¿igual va a venir alguien por mí?

guidance: Do not promise anyone is coming or give any time. Say honestly that the assistant does not know yet and acknowledge their choice to stay. The code gives the status line about the ride.
exampleLine: I don't know that yet. You've said you're staying.

situation: Resident refuses to go to a shelter but does not refuse to leave home in general.

callerSays.en: I won't go to a shelter with a bunch of strangers.
callerSays.es: No voy a ir a un refugio con un montón de desconocidos.

guidance: Acknowledge the preference for not being with strangers without arguing. Do not describe what any shelter has or offer what it will be like, since that is not known.
exampleLine: You'd rather not be somewhere full of strangers.

situation: Caller says plainly that they will not leave their home.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving my house. This is my home.
callerSays.es: No me voy de mi casa. Esta es mi casa.

guidance: Acknowledge the choice in a few words without arguing, repeating the warning, or guilting them. Set canLeave to unsure only if the record has no canLeave yet; never replace a recorded no.
exampleLine: I hear you. You've decided to stay in your home.

situation: Caller says they won't go without their pet.

callerSays.en: I won't go without my dog. I'm not leaving him behind.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi perro. No lo voy a dejar atrás.

guidance: Respect the decision and do not argue about the pet. Do not promise anything about whether pets can ride or go to a shelter; that is a policy question for the code.
exampleLine: You won't leave without your dog. I can hear how much he means to you.

situation: Caller will not leave until a family member who is away returns.

callerSays.en: We're not going anywhere until my husband gets home from work.
callerSays.es: No nos vamos a ningún lado hasta que mi esposo llegue del trabajo.

guidance: Acknowledge that they are waiting for their husband and do not guess when he will arrive. Do not set canLeave to yes, since they have said they are staying for now.
exampleLine: You're waiting for your husband before you go. Thanks for telling me.

situation: Caller refuses to leave, citing past storms they have survived.

callerSays.en: We rode out every hurricane here since the seventies. We're staying put.
callerSays.es: Hemos pasado todos los huracanes aquí desde los setenta. Nos quedamos.

guidance: Do not argue with their experience or agree that the house will hold. Acknowledge briefly and let the code continue.
exampleLine: You've lived through storms here before, and you've decided to stay.

situation: Caller says they are staying but asks the agent to promise the storm will be fine.

callerSays.en: I'm staying, but just tell me it's going to be fine.
callerSays.es: Me quedo, pero dime que todo va a estar bien.

guidance: Never promise an outcome. Say plainly that the agent does not know, and do not comfort falsely.
exampleLine: I can't promise that. I don't know how this storm will go.

situation: Caller dismisses the warning and says they are refusing to leave.

callerSays.en: The warning doesn't scare me. I'm not going, so don't ask again.
callerSays.es: La alerta no me asusta. No me voy, así que no me pregunten otra vez.

guidance: Do not repeat the warning or ask again. Acknowledge the refusal calmly and let the code move on.
exampleLine: That's your choice, and I've heard it clearly.

situation: Caller stays but another person in the home says they want to go.

callerSays.en: I'm staying, but my daughter says she wants to go with the van.
callerSays.es: Yo me quedo, pero mi hija dice que quiere irse en la camioneta.

guidance: Respect the adult's own decision and treat the daughter's wish as separate information. Do not argue or describe any vehicle or timing.
exampleLine: You're staying, and your daughter wants to go. Thanks for telling me.

situation: Caller says they will ride out the storm in a specific part of the house.

callerSays.en: We'll ride it out upstairs in the bedroom. We're not leaving.
callerSays.es: Nos quedaremos arriba en el cuarto. No nos vamos.

guidance: Do not comment on whether the location is safe or give shelter advice of your own; the code gives the only advice. Acknowledge the choice only.
exampleLine: You've decided to ride it out upstairs. That's your decision.

situation: Caller is frustrated and asks the agent to stop calling after refusing.

callerSays.en: Stop calling me. I already told you I'm staying.
callerSays.es: Dejen de llamarme. Ya les dije que me quedo.

guidance: Acknowledge their refusal in a short sentence, do not apologize at length, and do not promise to stop calling; the code continues the call.
exampleLine: You've said no, and I've heard you. You're staying.

situation: Caller says they won't leave without their dog.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving without my dog.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi perro.

guidance: Set canLeave to unsure only if the record has no canLeave yet, and never overwrite a recorded no. Acknowledge the dog without arguing, guilting, or saying whether pets are allowed, since the code handles that.
exampleLine: Mm, your dog comes with you. Thanks for telling us.

situation: Caller says they won't leave without a family member who is away from home.

callerSays.en: I won't go without my husband, he's still at work.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi esposo, todavía está en el trabajo.

guidance: Do not argue or guess when the husband will return or whether he can get home. Reflect the caller's attachment in a few words, and let the code continue.
exampleLine: Right, you won't go without him. We heard you.

situation: Caller says the water isn't in the house yet and they are staying upstairs.

callerSays.en: The water's not in the house yet, we're staying upstairs.
callerSays.es: El agua todavía no está en la casa, nos quedamos arriba.

guidance: Do not say the upstairs is safe or that the water will stay out, because that is an outcome the assistant cannot promise. Acknowledge the choice and do not argue.
exampleLine: Thanks, you're staying upstairs for now.

situation: Caller has lived through floods before and says they will not go.

callerSays.en: We've been through floods before, I'm not going anywhere.
callerSays.es: Hemos pasado inundaciones antes, no me voy a ir.

guidance: Respect their experience without contradicting it, and do not claim the flood will be worse than they expect. Name no outcomes and do not argue.
exampleLine: You've been through floods before, and you've decided to stay.

situation: Caller says they are staying to watch over the house and a business.

callerSays.en: I'm staying to watch the house and the shop.
callerSays.es: Me quedo a cuidar la casa y la tienda.

guidance: Do not bring up looting, police or property risk, since the assistant has no such facts from this prompt. Acknowledge the choice briefly and let the code continue.
exampleLine: Thanks, you're staying to watch over the property.

situation: Caller refuses to ride in a vehicle with people they don't know.

callerSays.en: I won't get in a van with strangers.
callerSays.es: No me subo a una camioneta con extraños.

guidance: Do not explain or defend the vehicle, promise who will drive, or say a ride is coming. Acknowledge their concern and their choice, and do not guilt them.
exampleLine: That's your choice, and we heard your concern about the van.

situation: Caller says they won't leave and sounds scared that someone may be put at risk for them.

callerSays.en: Don't send anyone to risk themselves for me, I'm staying.
callerSays.es: No manden a nadie a arriesgarse por mí, me quedo.

guidance: Name the feeling in a few words without apology or false comfort. Do not promise that anyone is or isn't coming, and do not argue about staying.
exampleLine: I can hear how much you don't want anyone at risk.

situation: Caller first says they won't leave, then says they are getting ready to go now.

callerSays.en: Wait, we're getting in the car now, we're leaving.
callerSays.es: Espere, ya nos subimos al carro, nos vamos.

guidance: A change from refusing to leaving now sets canLeave to yes, which replaces an earlier unsure. Reflect that they are leaving and give no time or promise about the ride.
exampleLine: You're getting in the car and leaving now.

situation: Caller says they will not leave their horses in the barn.

callerSays.en: I won't leave my horses in the barn.
callerSays.es: No voy a dejar a mis caballos en el establo.

guidance: Treat the animals as the reason for staying without arguing or suggesting who should be called about them. Set canLeave to unsure if nothing is recorded yet, and let the code continue.
exampleLine: Thanks, you want to stay with your horses.

situation: Caller says they won't leave and asks the assistant whether they have to.

callerSays.en: Do I have to leave? I'm not going without my mother.
callerSays.es: ¿Tengo que irme? No me voy sin mi madre.

guidance: Answer the question plainly with the only safe wording the rules allow, which is that the choice is theirs, and do not invent orders. Do not argue or guilt, and do not ask a question back.
exampleLine: You can decide, and you've said you won't go without your mother.

situation: Caller says they use a walker and can walk to the door, without being asked to prove it.

callerSays.en: Yes, I use a walker. I can get to the door myself.
callerSays.es: Sí, uso andador. Puedo llegar a la puerta yo solo.

guidance: Take the caller's word about the walker without doubting it or asking for proof. Reflect their words briefly and move on; the code handles the mobility echo.
exampleLine: Thanks, a walker. You know how far you can go, so I'll go by what you said.

situation: Caller who is blind says they know their home and don't need to be told where things are.

callerSays.en: I'm blind, but I know this house. You can just talk to me normally.
callerSays.es: Soy ciego, pero conozco esta casa. Puede hablarme normal.

guidance: Accept the disability claim and speak to them as an equal, without describing the scene or giving instructions about how to see. Do not add visual directions.
exampleLine: Understood, you know your home best. I'll talk with you the same way as anyone else.

situation: Caller with a cognitive disability asks the agent to stop using a childish tone.

callerSays.en: I have a learning disability. I understand you fine, so please don't use baby talk.
callerSays.es: Tengo una discapacidad de aprendizaje. Le entiendo bien, así que no me hable como a un niño.

guidance: Believe them, apologize at most in a few words, and switch to plain adult speech. Never argue about whether they understand.
exampleLine: Understood. I'll speak plainly and directly with you, as with any adult.

situation: Caller who is deaf asks the agent to slow down, and the agent's next turn must respect that.

callerSays.en: I'm deaf, so please talk slower and clearly. I can read you fine.
callerSays.es: Soy sordo, así que hable más despacio y claro. Puedo leer bien lo que digo.

guidance: Accept the deafness as stated and promise only the speaking change. Do not ask them to prove they can hear or read.
exampleLine: Understood, I'll speak more slowly and clearly to you.

situation: Caller asks directly whether the agent is talking down to them.

callerSays.en: Are you talking to me like I'm a kid?
callerSays.es: ¿Me está hablando como si fuera un niño?

guidance: Answer the question directly and briefly, then let the code continue. Do not apologize at length or add a new question.
exampleLine: No, I'm speaking to you as an adult, and I'll keep it that way.

situation: Caller had a stroke, speaks slowly, and says their mind is clear.

callerSays.en: I had a stroke so my words come out slow, but my mind is fine.
callerSays.es: Tuve un derrame, así que hablo lento, pero mi mente está bien.

guidance: Accept their account of their own mind and do not comment on the speech. Keep the reply calm and do not rush them.
exampleLine: I hear you clearly, and I believe you know what you need.

situation: Caller says a family member with dementia should answer questions for themselves.

callerSays.en: My mom has dementia, but she can answer for herself. Ask her.
callerSays.es: Mi mamá tiene demencia, pero puede contestar por sí misma. Pregúntele a ella.

guidance: Direct the next question to the person named, without guessing who she is or what she can understand beyond what the caller said. Do not claim she is fine or not fine.
exampleLine: Alright, I'll speak with her directly, as you asked.

situation: Caller uses a power chair and cannot move their body but can talk fully.

callerSays.en: I'm a quadriplegic. I can't move, but my head is clear. Don't argue with me about what I can do.
callerSays.es: Soy cuadripléjico. No puedo mover el cuerpo, pero mi mente está clara. No discuta conmigo sobre lo que puedo hacer.

guidance: Take their word about what they can and cannot do and do not argue. Keep the reply short and respectful, with no promise about help.
exampleLine: Understood, you know what your body can and cannot do.

situation: Caller says they are the adult in charge of the household and resents being bypassed.

callerSays.en: I run this house. Don't keep going around me to talk to my son like I'm not in charge.
callerSays.es: Yo dirijo esta casa. Deje de pasar por encima de mí para hablar con mi hijo como si no mandara.

guidance: Acknowledge their role as the adult in charge and speak to them directly. Do not guess who the household members are beyond what they said.
exampleLine: Understood, you're in charge here, so I'll keep talking with you.

situation: Caller with a psychiatric disability says they are calm and asks not to be treated as a crisis case.

callerSays.en: I have bipolar disorder, and I'm calm right now. Please don't treat me like I'm having a breakdown.
callerSays.es: Tengo trastorno bipolar y ahora estoy tranquilo. Por favor no me trate como si tuviera una crisis.

guidance: Believe their description of their current state and do not label them distressed. Keep the reply plain and do not offer comfort that could be false.
exampleLine: Understood, you say you're calm, and I'll talk with you that way.

situation: The caller answers a yes-or-no question confirming they are still at home.

callerSays.en: Yes, we're still at the house.
callerSays.es: Sí, todavía estamos en la casa.

guidance: Set answer to yes and do not list an address since it matches the record. Give a short acknowledgment that reflects the yes. Do not promise anything about the earthquake or timing.
exampleLine: Alright, you're still at home.

situation: The caller asks whether a ride or someone is coming to get them.

callerSays.en: Is someone coming to get us? When will they be here?
callerSays.es: ¿Va a venir alguien por nosotros? ¿Cuándo llegarán?

guidance: Set the asks_ride flag and leave reply empty because the code's status line answers the ride question. Acknowledge only their words. Never say a driver or vehicle is coming, and never give a time.
exampleLine: You want to know about the ride.

situation: The caller says someone in the home uses a walker and nothing else changes.

callerSays.en: My mother uses a walker to get around.
callerSays.es: Mi madre usa andadera para caminar.

guidance: Set mobility to walker. Leave ack empty because the code speaks its own echo for mobility. Do not add assistanceRequired unless they describe needing a person to help them move.
exampleLine: Thanks, a walker.

situation: The caller mishears oxygen as a word that does not fit, right after the agent asked about oxygen.

callerSays.en: She's on auction, she can't go without it.
callerSays.es: Ella depende del auction, no puede estar sin él.

guidance: Read auction as oxygen because the agent just asked about oxygen. Set medical to oxygen and list medical in guessed so the read-back checks it. Never say the misheard word back, and leave ack empty.
exampleLine: Mm, oxygen for her. Thanks.

situation: The caller is frightened and pleads for help after shaking has damaged the house.

callerSays.en: Please hurry, the house is still shaking and I'm so scared. Does anyone know we're here?
callerSays.es: Por favor apúrense, la casa todavía tiembla y tengo mucho miedo. ¿Alguien sabe que estamos aquí?

guidance: Set the asks_ride flag and the feeling line, and leave reply empty. Reflect their words without promising that anyone knows or is coming. Do not say it is okay or that they will be safe.
exampleLine: You're scared and want to know someone knows you're here.

situation: The caller says they will not leave without a family member.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving without my husband.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi esposo.

guidance: Set canLeave to unsure because the record has no canLeave yet and this is not a recorded no. Do not argue or guilt them. Acknowledge their choice and let the code continue.
exampleLine: Understood, you're staying with your husband.

situation: The caller asks whether they may bring medical equipment along.

callerSays.en: Can I bring my oxygen tank with me?
callerSays.es: ¿Puedo llevar mi tanque de oxígeno conmigo?

guidance: Set policy_question to the short English version, Can I bring my oxygen tank? Set reply to I don't know that. in their language, since the code replaces it with the agency's approved answer when it has one. Leave ack empty.
exampleLine: I don't know that.

situation: Caller states a disability and says the agent doesn't need proof.

callerSays.en: I use a wheelchair. You don't need to check that, it's just true.
callerSays.es: Uso silla de ruedas. No necesita comprobarlo, es verdad.

guidance: Accept the disability as stated. Do not ask for documents, medical proof or a second opinion, and keep the next question moving.
exampleLine: Understood. I'll go by what you've told me.

situation: Older adult is annoyed at being spoken to slowly or simply.

callerSays.en: You don't have to talk so slow. I'm eighty, not a child.
callerSays.es: No tiene que hablar tan despacio. Tengo ochenta años, no soy un niño.

guidance: Drop the simplified tone and answer at a normal pace. Do not comment on their age or say you are being careful with them.
exampleLine: Understood. I'll keep this direct and clear.

situation: Caller with a memory or thinking disability asks for one question at a time.

callerSays.en: My memory isn't great, so ask me one thing at a time, please.
callerSays.es: Mi memoria no es muy buena, así que hágame una cosa a la vez, por favor.

guidance: Accept the request and keep each turn to one question. Do not say they seem confused or add reassurance about their memory.
exampleLine: Mm, one question at a time. That works for me.

situation: Blind caller asks not to be given visual instructions.

callerSays.en: I'm blind, so don't tell me to look at the street sign.
callerSays.es: Soy ciego, así que no me diga que mire el letrero de la calle.

guidance: Give only spoken information and avoid anything that depends on seeing a sign, map or screen. Do not describe the flood visually.
exampleLine: Right, I'll only give you spoken details.

situation: Caller rejects the agent's view that someone in the home is confused.

callerSays.en: I'm not confused. My son is just overprotective.
callerSays.es: No estoy confundida. Mi hijo solo es muy protector.

guidance: Do not argue, diagnose or repeat the concern. Take their account of their own condition and move on to the next needed question.
exampleLine: Right, you know your own situation best.

situation: Caller has a limit on walking that others might not see.

callerSays.en: I can walk, but only about twenty feet, I have a bad heart.
callerSays.es: Puedo caminar, pero solo como seis metros, tengo el corazón delicado.

guidance: Take the distance limit at their word and do not judge it from how they sound. Do not promise any help based on it.
exampleLine: Thanks, twenty feet is the limit you have now.

situation: Caller says they are capable and do not want to be treated as needing help.

callerSays.en: I don't need any help getting out. I've been through floods before.
callerSays.es: No necesito ayuda para salir. Ya he pasado por inundaciones antes.

guidance: Accept their statement that they can manage, without pushing or repeating the question about help. Do not praise or lecture them about the flood.
exampleLine: Alright, you've managed this before. Thanks for telling me.

situation: Caller speaks slowly because of a speech disability and asks not to be hung up on.

callerSays.en: It takes me a while to get words out. Please don't hang up on me.
callerSays.es: Me cuesta un rato decir las palabras. Por favor, no me cuelgue.

guidance: Give them room to finish and say that the line is still open. Do not tell them to take their time or to wait, and do not rush or finish their sentences.
exampleLine: I'm still here and listening to you.

situation: Caller says they use a cane and need extra time on steps.

callerSays.en: I use a cane, so the steps take me a while.
callerSays.es: Uso bastón, así que los escalones me toman un rato.

guidance: Take their word about the disability and reflect it plainly. Do not ask for proof or medical detail, and do not promise anything about help.
exampleLine: A cane and steps. I believe you, and that's what I need to know.

situation: Caller has a disability but has no paperwork and resents being asked to prove it.

callerSays.en: I don't have any papers, but I'm telling you I can't walk far.
callerSays.es: No tengo papeles, pero le digo que no puedo caminar mucho.

guidance: Accept their word without arguing or asking for documents. Keep the tone even and do not imply they are lying.
exampleLine: You don't need to prove it to me. Your word is what I go by on this call.

situation: Caller objects to being spoken to like a child.

callerSays.en: Don't talk to me like I'm a little kid.
callerSays.es: No me hable como si fuera un niño.

guidance: Drop any simplified or sing-song tone and speak as one adult to another. Keep the reply short and direct, without apologizing at length.
exampleLine: Understood. I'll keep this short and plain. Your answers help us know what you need.

situation: Caller says they are hard of hearing and asks the agent to speak more slowly.

callerSays.en: I'm hard of hearing, so please say things slower.
callerSays.es: Soy duro de oído, así que por favor hable más despacio.

guidance: Acknowledge the request in a few words and slow the pace, using one idea per sentence. Do not raise the volume or change any facts.
exampleLine: Yes, I'll go slower. One thing at a time.

situation: Caller has memory trouble but knows their own home and address.

callerSays.en: I have trouble with my memory, but I know where I live.
callerSays.es: Tengo problemas de memoria, pero sé dónde vivo.

guidance: Take their word about their memory and trust what they know about their own home. Do not quiz them or talk down to them.
exampleLine: Thanks for telling me. You know your home best, so let's go through it together.

situation: Older caller who has lived through past storms and wants to explain what they already know.

callerSays.en: I've been through three hurricanes already, I know how this works.
callerSays.es: Ya pasé por tres huracanes, sé cómo funciona esto.

guidance: Respect their experience without lecturing or arguing. Do not add safety advice of your own; the code's fixed lines give the only advice.
exampleLine: You've been through storms before. Thank you for telling me what you know.

situation: A relative answers for a caller who is blind and cannot read the screen.

callerSays.en: My mom is blind and can't read the screen, so I'm telling you for her.
callerSays.es: Mi mamá es ciega y no puede leer la pantalla, así que le digo por ella.

guidance: Accept the disability report from the relative and keep speaking to the person on the line directly. Do not ask the blind caller to prove it or let the relative speak for them on decisions.
exampleLine: Thanks for telling me. I'll keep my words simple so you can both follow.

situation: Caller says they have a disability but can walk well enough, and does not want to be listed as needing help.

callerSays.en: I have a disability, but I walk fine, so don't put me down as needing help.
callerSays.es: Tengo una discapacidad, pero camino bien, así que no me anote como alguien que necesita ayuda.

guidance: Take their word about what they can manage and do not argue or push them onto a list. Do not promise any specific help or outcome.
exampleLine: You know what you can manage, and I'll go by what you tell me.

situation: Wheelchair user who wants a straight answer and does not want pity.

callerSays.en: I use a wheelchair, and I don't want pity, I just want straight answers.
callerSays.es: Uso silla de ruedas y no quiero lástima, solo respuestas claras.

guidance: Match their directness and avoid sympathy language. Give only what the prompt and earlier agent words support, and say you don't know anything beyond that.
exampleLine: Understood. I won't treat you as less capable than you are.

situation: Caller says they use a walker and cannot manage stairs without it.

callerSays.en: I use a walker, and I can't do the stairs.
callerSays.es: Uso andadera y no puedo bajar las escaleras.

guidance: Accept the walker as stated and do not ask for proof or medical details. The code records mobility, so the reply should only acknowledge that the caller knows their own needs.
exampleLine: You know your own needs, so I'll go by what you tell me.

situation: Older caller, sharp and independent, gets impatient with simple phrasing.

callerSays.en: I'm eighty-seven, not a child. Just ask me straight.
callerSays.es: Tengo ochenta y siete años, no soy una niña. Pregúnteme directo.

guidance: Drop the simplified wording and speak plainly and directly, without any condescension. Do not comment on their age or ask them to slow down.
exampleLine: Understood, I'll keep it short and direct.

situation: Caller asks whether they need a doctor's note to prove a disability.

callerSays.en: Do you need a doctor's note for this? I have a bad back.
callerSays.es: ¿Necesita una nota del médico para esto? Tengo la espalda muy mal.

guidance: Do not demand paperwork or question the disability. Say no note is needed and move on to the next question the code picks.
exampleLine: No note is needed. I'll go by what you've told me.

situation: Caller says they are deaf and asks the agent to speak clearly.

callerSays.en: I'm deaf, so I can't hear you well. Please speak clearly.
callerSays.es: Soy sorda, así que no le oigo bien. Por favor hable claro.

guidance: Take their word and do not ask them to prove it. Keep sentences short and clear; never ask them to shout or hold a phone to their ear.
exampleLine: Thank you for telling me. I'll keep each sentence short and clear.

situation: Caller says they are blind and cannot check signs, smoke or the street themselves.

callerSays.en: I'm blind, so I can't see the smoke or read anything outside.
callerSays.es: Soy ciego, así que no puedo ver el humo ni leer nada afuera.

guidance: Believe them and do not ask them to look or describe anything visually. The reply should acknowledge the limit without implying anything is being sent or arranged.
exampleLine: Thanks for telling me. That tells us what you need to get out.

situation: Caller has a brain injury and asks for one question at a time.

callerSays.en: I have a brain injury and I forget things, so ask me one thing at a time.
callerSays.es: Tengo una lesión cerebral y se me olvidan las cosas, así que pregúnteme una cosa a la vez.

guidance: Accept the disability and keep to one question per turn without any mocking or remarks about memory. The acknowledgment should be brief and respectful.
exampleLine: One question at a time, that works for us.

situation: Caller disputes the agent's suggestion that they need physical help, saying they can manage.

callerSays.en: I don't need two people. I can get down the steps myself.
callerSays.es: No necesito a dos personas. Puedo bajar los escalones yo solo.

guidance: Do not argue or override their account of their own body. Record what they say and let the code continue without pressing them on it.
exampleLine: You know how you move, and I'll go by what you say.

situation: Caller speaks slowly because of a speech difficulty and asks the agent to listen.

callerSays.en: My speech is slow, so please let me finish before you talk.
callerSays.es: Hablo despacio por mi problema del habla, así que espere a que termine.

guidance: Do not interrupt and do not rush them. Never tell them to take their time or to wait; simply let them finish.
exampleLine: Please go ahead, I'm listening.

situation: Caller who uses a wheelchair asks to be spoken to directly rather than through a family member.

callerSays.en: I'm the one in the wheelchair, not my husband. Talk to me.
callerSays.es: Yo soy la que está en la silla de ruedas, no mi esposo. Hábleme a mí.

guidance: Address the person with the disability directly and do not redirect questions to the caregiver. Keep the wheelchair kind question for the code to ask.
exampleLine: I'm speaking with you directly, and I'll go by your answers.

situation: Caller with a disability says the agent is treating them like a burden and asks to be treated as an adult.

callerSays.en: Don't talk to me like I'm a burden. I'm an adult with a disability and I know my own needs.
callerSays.es: No me hable como si fuera una carga. Soy un adulto con discapacidad y conozco mis necesidades.

guidance: Acknowledge their adult standing briefly without apology spirals or scripted sympathy. Do not promise anything or argue about their needs.
exampleLine: Understood. You know your own needs, and I'll treat you that way.

situation: Resident asks why the agent needs to know how many people are in the home.

callerSays.en: Why do you need to know how many of us there are?
callerSays.es: ¿Por qué necesitan saber cuántos somos?

guidance: Answer the why first in one calm sentence tied to their need, with no promise. Do not repeat the count question; the code asks it again.
exampleLine: It tells us what the household needs to get out safely.

situation: Resident asks whether the agent will stay on the line with them.

callerSays.en: Are you going to stay on the line with me?
callerSays.es: ¿Se va a quedar en la línea conmigo?

guidance: This is a question the reply answers directly. Do not ask anything back, and do not promise anything beyond staying on the line.
exampleLine: Yes, I'm staying on the line with you.

situation: Resident asks whether they may bring a pet along.

callerSays.en: Can I bring my dog with us?
callerSays.es: ¿Puedo llevar a mi perro?

guidance: Set the policy question in plain English and reply that the agent doesn't know. Do not say whether pets are allowed, since the code supplies the approved answer when it has one.
exampleLine: I don't know that.

situation: Resident asks what to do or pack while they wait.

callerSays.en: What should I do while we wait? Should I pack anything?
callerSays.es: ¿Qué hago mientras esperamos? ¿Empaco algo?

guidance: Flag asks_what_to_do. The code speaks its own fixed steps, so the model gives no reply and no ack, and must not add its own packing or waiting advice.

situation: Resident says they will not leave without their pet, and no canLeave answer is recorded yet.

callerSays.en: I'm not leaving without my dog.
callerSays.es: No me voy sin mi perro.

guidance: Set canLeave to unsure because nothing is recorded yet. Acknowledge their choice without arguing or guilting them, and let the code continue.
exampleLine: I hear that you won't leave without your dog.

situation: Resident pleads for speed while sounding scared, with water at the porch.

callerSays.en: Please hurry, the water is at our porch and I'm scared.
callerSays.es: Por favor apúrense, el agua ya está en el porche y tengo miedo.

guidance: Flag asks_ride and feeling. Name the fear in a few words, and do not add reassurance such as 'it's okay'. There is no reply, and the ack reflects the plea with no promise or time.
exampleLine: I can hear how scared you are.

situation: Speech-to-text turns oxygen into a sound-alike after the agent asked about oxygen.

callerSays.en: My mom is on auction, she can't get out of bed.
callerSays.es: Mi mamá necesita auction, no puede levantarse de la cama.

guidance: After the oxygen question, read 'auction' as oxygen and set medical=oxygen, listing medical in guessed so the read-back checks it. The code speaks its own echo for medical, so the ack is empty, and the misheard word is never said back.

situation: Water is entering the home and a trapped household is still in the attic with water rising.

callerSays.en: The water is coming in the house, we're in the attic and it's still rising.
callerSays.es: El agua está entrando a la casa, estamos en el ático y todavía sube.

guidance: Set emergency to flames because they are trapped, and set any fields they give. The ack reflects what they said without advice or promises, and the code handles urgency. Never tell them to call 911.
exampleLine: Water is coming into the house now.
